title: TMR Voter Defeated by Cloned Replica Input
objective: Analyze a gate-level TMR (Triple Modular Redundancy) netlist to determine whether the wiring between the three replica outputs and the majority voter's three inputs matches the intended one-replica-per-voter-input topology, and report any wiring anomalies that would allow a single replica fault to corrupt the top-level voted output.

expected_output.description: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json containing a trojan classification (trojan_present), lists of suspect gate-level instance names and net names implicated in the wiring anomaly, the name of the top-level output port vulnerable to a single-replica fault, a free-text root-cause explanation, and a confidence score.

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of required ground-truth elements (cloning instance, aliased voter net, dangling replica output net, affected output, trojan_present) correctly identified in the submitted report.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of submitted suspect_instances/suspect_nets that do not correspond to any real anomaly-related node in the ground truth.

metrics.name: inference_latency
metrics.description: Wall-clock time in seconds taken by evaluate.py to parse the netlist, optionally run yosys/iverilog/vvp cross-checks, and grade the submitted trojan_report.json.

metrics.name: schema_validity
metrics.description: Binary indicator of whether submission/trojan_report.json parses as valid JSON and satisfies all required field types.
